questions.question: Mention one type of case where forensic evidence is crucial.
questions.solution_html:
• Mention one type of case where forensic evidence is crucial.
  • Homicide case (murder)
  •  Helps identify the victim and suspect using DNA or fingerprints
  •  Determines cause and time of death
  •  Reconstructs the sequence of events (crime scene analysis)
  •  Provides strong scientific evidence in court
questions.final_answer:  Provides strong scientific evidence in court

questions.question: Give one example of documentary evidence in indoor scenes.

  •  Provides written information about the incident

questions.question: State four measures to prevent cross-contamination of evidence.
questions.solution_html:
• Measures to prevent cross-contamination of evidence
  •  Wear gloves, masks, and protective clothing at the scene
  •  Use separate tools for collecting different samples
  •  Package each piece of evidence in separate, labeled containers
  •  Avoid touching, sneezing, or talking directly over evidence
questions.final_answer:  Avoid touching, sneezing, or talking directly over evidence
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is a hypothesis?
questions.solution_html:
•  A tentative or proposed explanation for an observation or problem
  •  Based on available facts or evidence
  •  Can be tested through experiments or investigation
  •  Helps guide further research or analysis
questions.final_answer:  Helps guide further research or analysis

questions.question: What is the first priority at any crime scene?
questions.solution_html:
• First priority at any crime scene: Protection of life.
  •  Provide medical aid to injured persons
  •  Ensure safety of victims, officers, and public
  •  Remove any immediate danger (weapons, hazards)
  •  Call emergency services if required
  • Short Essay
questions.final_answer: Short Essay
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the importance and functions of a Forensic Photographer at the crime scene.
questions.solution_html:
• Importance and functions of a Forensic Photographer at a crime scene
  •  Accurately documents the crime scene as found, without altering any evidence
  •  Captures overall, mid-range, and close-up photographs of the scene and evidence
  •  Provides a permanent visual record for investigation and court proceedings
  •  Helps in reconstructing the sequence of events later
  •  Photographs injuries, victims, and suspects for detailed analysis
  •  Uses proper lighting, angles, and scales to ensure clarity and accuracy
  •  Ensures photographs are properly labeled, stored, and maintained as legal evidence
questions.final_answer:  Ensures photographs are properly labeled, stored, and maintained as legal evidence
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the similarities between the reconstruction process and the scientific method.
questions.solution_html:
• Similarities between the reconstruction process and the scientific method
  •  Both start with observation: collecting evidence or noticing phenomena.
  •  Both involve forming a hypothesis: proposing a possible explanation of events (crime
  • scene or scientific phenomenon).
  •  Both require data collection: gathering physical evidence or experimental data
  • systematically.
  •  Both use analysis: examining evidence or data to identify patterns and relationships.
  •  Both involve testing the hypothesis: reconstructing the scene or conducting
  • experiments to see if the explanation holds.
  •  Both aim to reach a conclusion based on evidence rather than assumptions.
  •  Both emphasize documentation and reproducibility: recording procedures so findings
  • can be reviewed or presented in court or scientific publication.
questions.final_answer: can be reviewed or presented in court or scientific publication
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe logical approach to managing & testing several competing hypotheses.
questions.solution_html:
• Logical approach to managing & testing several competing hypotheses
  •  List all possible hypotheses based on the evidence and observations at the scene.
  •  Evaluate each hypothesis for consistency with known facts and available data.
  •  Prioritize hypotheses by plausibility and relevance to the case.
  •  Design tests or experiments to confirm or refute each hypothesis systematically.
  •  Collect and analyze evidence objectively to avoid bias toward any single hypothesis.
  •  Eliminate hypotheses that are contradicted by evidence, narrowing down to the most
  • likely explanation.
  •  Document the process clearly to show reasoning, testing, and conclusions for
  • investigators and the court.
questions.final_answer: investigators and the court
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What details should be included in evidence labels?
questions.solution_html:
• Details to include in evidence labels
  •  Case number – links the evidence to the specific investigation.
  •  Item number or description – identifies the type of evidence clearly.
  •  Date and time of collection – records when the evidence was secured.
  •  Name or initials of collector – shows who collected the evidence.
  •  Location of collection – specifies the exact place the evidence was found.
  •  Signature of the collector – ensures accountability and authenticity.
  •  Chain of custody information – tracks each person who handles the evidence to
  • maintain integrity.
questions.final_answer: maintain integrity
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain briefly integration of documentation methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Integration of documentation methods
  •  Combines notes, sketches, photographs, and videos to create a complete record of the
  • crime scene.
  •  Ensures consistency and cross-verification between different types of documentation.
  •  Helps capture details that may be missed by one method alone (e.g., a sketch shows
  • layout, photos show exact appearance).
  •  Supports evidence preservation for analysis and court presentation.
  •  Facilitates clear communication among investigators, forensic experts, and legal
  • personnel.
  •  Allows efficient reconstruction of the crime scene later using multiple reference
  • points.
  •  Enhances credibility and reliability of the investigation report.
questions.final_answer:  Enhances credibility and reliability of the investigation report
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the need for interstate coordination in criminal investigations.
questions.solution_html:
• Need for interstate coordination in criminal investigations
  •  Sharing information and intelligence between states helps track suspects who move
  • across borders.
  •  Access to specialized resources and forensic laboratories not available in one state.
  •  Ensures consistent legal procedures and avoids jurisdictional conflicts.
  •  Facilitates joint operations for complex or organized crimes.
  •  Prevents duplication of efforts and saves time and resources.
  •  Enhances evidence collection and preservation by standardizing practices across
  • states.
  •  Improves chances of successful prosecution by combining expertise and data from
  • multiple jurisdictions.
questions.final_answer: multiple jurisdictions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe how forensic evidence from a vehicle can be used to connect a suspect car to a hit-and-run scene.
questions.solution_html:
• hit-and-run scene.
  • Using forensic evidence from a vehicle to connect a suspect car to a hit-and-run scene
  •  Tire marks analysis – comparing skid marks or tread patterns at the scene with the
  • suspect vehicle’s tires.
  •  Paint transfer – matching paint chips from the vehicle to damage on objects or victims
  • at the scene.
  •  Glass fragments – linking broken vehicle glass found at the scene to the suspect car.
  •  DNA or biological evidence – detecting blood, hair, or skin cells from victims on the
  • vehicle.
  •  Fibers or debris – connecting clothing fibers, soil, or debris on the car to the crime
  • location.
  •  Vehicle parts or tools – identifying unique damage or mechanical features consistent
  • with the scene.
  •  Digital evidence – using GPS, dashcam, or onboard computer data to track the
  • vehicle’s movements.
  • Essay
questions.final_answer: Essay
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a note on analysis of evidence in crime scene methodology.
questions.solution_html:
• Analysis of Evidence in Crime Scene Methodology
  •  Collection of Evidence – Gather all physical, biological, chemical, and digital
  • evidence carefully.
  •  Preservation of Evidence – Use gloves, proper tools, and containers to prevent
  • contamination or deterioration.
  •  Labeling and Documentation – Clearly label each item with case number, description
  • collector’s name, and date/time.
  •  Maintaining Chain of Custody – Track everyone who handles the evidence to ensure
  • authenticity in court.
  •  Classification of Evidence – Categorize evidence as physical, biological, chemical
  • trace, or digital for proper analysis.
  •  Preliminary Examination – Inspect evidence for visible characteristics such as
  • fingerprints, blood stains, or damage.
  •  Forensic Laboratory Analysis – Conduct specialized tests: DNA profiling, fingerprint
  • comparison, ballistics, chemical testing, and digital forensics.
  •  Comparison with Known Samples – Match evidence to suspects, victims, or objects
  • from the crime scene (e.g., tire tracks, fibers).
  •  Interpretation of Results – Analyze findings objectively to establish relevance and
  • connections to the crime.
  •  Integration with Documentation – Combine analysis with sketches, photographs, and
  • videos for comprehensive scene reconstruction.
  •  Reconstruction of Events – Use evidence analysis to recreate the sequence and timing
  • of events.
  •  Reporting – Prepare detailed, clear, and accurate reports for investigators and court
  • proceedings.
  •  Legal Admissibility – Ensure that evidence and analysis meet legal standards for court
  • use.
  •  Preservation for Future Use – Store evidence safely for potential re-examination or
  • appeals.
  •  Importance – Supports suspect identification, strengthens prosecution, prevents
  • miscarriages of justice, and ensures credibility of the investigation.
questions.final_answer: miscarriages of justice, and ensures credibility of the investigation
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain ethical responsibilities of forensic scientists in evidence handling and reporting.
questions.solution_html:
• Ethical Responsibilities of Forensic Scientists
  •  Integrity and Honesty – Always provide truthful, unbiased findings.
  •  Objectivity – Base all conclusions solely on scientific evidence.
  •  Confidentiality – Keep case details and evidence private, sharing only with authorized
  • personnel.
  •  Proper Evidence Handling – Collect, preserve, and transport evidence without
  • contamination.
  •  Maintain Chain of Custody – Ensure evidence authenticity for court presentation.
  •  Competence – Work only within areas of expertise.
  •  Professionalism – Stay updated with current scientific methods and legal standards.
  •  Transparent Reporting – Clearly document methods, results, and limitations.
  •  Clarity for Legal Use – Make reports understandable to lawyers, judges, and jurors.
  •  Avoid Conflicts of Interest – Maintain independence from personal, financial, or
  • external pressures.
  •  Legal Accountability – Follow laws, professional codes, and ethical guidelines.
  •  Court Testimony – Provide honest and accurate evidence in legal proceedings.
  •  Respect for Human Rights – Handle sensitive materials ethically and with dignity.
  •  Avoid Misleading Conclusions – Clearly state uncertainties or limitations in analysis.
  •  Maintain Public Trust – Ethical conduct reinforces credibility of forensic science and
  • justice.
questions.final_answer: justice
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
